problem_text:
A city planner needs to distribute a fixed budget across 13 infrastructure projects to maximize the total projected community benefit.  
The characteristics of each project are:  
* Project A: projected benefit 0.114, disruption index 0.147, allocation bounds [0.013, 0.624]  
* Project B: projected benefit 0.101, disruption index 0.026, allocation bounds [0.053, 0.654]  
* Project C: projected benefit 0.050, disruption index 0.234, allocation bounds [0.017, 0.574]  
* Project D: projected benefit 0.174, disruption index 0.162, allocation bounds [0.004, 0.749]  
* Project E: projected benefit 0.043, disruption index 0.299, allocation bounds [0.036, 0.826]  
* Project F: projected benefit 0.062, disruption index 0.040, allocation bounds [0.092, 0.561]  
* Project G: projected benefit 0.065, disruption index 0.189, allocation bounds [0.086, 0.684]  
* Project H: projected benefit 0.154, disruption index 0.034, allocation bounds [0.047, 0.620]  
* Project I: projected benefit 0.155, disruption index 0.280, allocation bounds [0.087, 0.845]  
* Project J: projected benefit 0.058, disruption index 0.123, allocation bounds [0.093, 0.589]  
* Project K: projected benefit 0.091, disruption index 0.077, allocation bounds [0.055, 0.436]  
* Project L: projected benefit 0.037, disruption index 0.224, allocation bounds [0.014, 0.354]  
* Project M: projected benefit 0.189, disruption index 0.139, allocation bounds [0.095, 0.485]  

Each project must receive a fraction of the total budget within its specified bounds, and the sum of all allocations must equal one.  
To ensure equitable regional coverage, the subset of projects in high-priority zones L = {A, D, F, I, J} must collectively receive at least 0.288 of the total budget.  
Additionally, the overall disruption index of the portfolio must not exceed 0.178, and the total projected benefit must be at least 0.096.  
Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes total projected benefit while satisfying all constraints.
